transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-10
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ravi Desai (Aquarelle), Kara Bennett (Aquarelle), Liam O'Neill (Aquarelle), Sofia Martinez (Aquarelle procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): cost spike in last billing period, higher tail-latency on weekday peaks, customer wants pilot + rollback plan, security artifacts requested.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. quick around the room?
[00:06] Ravi Desai: hi maya, ravI here. we'll kick off. thanks.
[00:11] Kara Bennett: Kara. good to see you all.
[00:13] Liam O'Neill: Liam joining, morning.
[00:16] Sofia Martinez: Sofia from procurement.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Awesome. Ethan and Priya from our side, they'll lead the tail-latency and cost bits. Jordan will handle the health/readout followups.
[00:26] Ethan Park: hey team. quick agenda: usage/cost trend, latency incidents, root causes we think, Dedicated vs Hosted cost modeling, pilot scope and next steps. sound OK?
[00:34] Ravi Desai: yep, that works. last billing cycle we saw a 28% increase in token consumption month-over-month; want to understand why and where to optimize.
[00:44] Maya Chen: understood. Kara, could you share what changed on your side? rollout, more users?
[00:48] Kara Bennett: yeah, we did expand a feature to 10% of prod traffic; it's a conversational assist that uses ~1.2k tokens per session on average. Also we had a couple of retrain pushes that made prompts longer. so both usage and per-request size increased.
[01:03] Ethan Park: that aligns with what we see — both mean tokens-per-request up and more small spikes. we also flagged an uptick in 99th percentile latency during your 11am-1pm PST window.
[01:13] Liam O'Neill: that 99th was visible in our graphs — garbage spikes, some requests hit cold KV cash — excuse me, KV cache — warmup didn't happen.
[01:22] Priya Nair: yeah KV cache sometimes transcribed as "KV cash" in earlier notes ha — but to be clear the runtime has an adaptive prefix caching; if there's a churn in model variants the cache miss rate goes up.
[01:34] Ravi Desai: do we know if those misses are due to rolling deploys or autoscale / preemption on the Dedicated pool?
[01:40] Ethan Park: preliminary look: mix of both. a couple of scheduled rollouts coincided with a traffic surge, and we saw one pod preempted during an aggressive scale event in your Dedicated pool. that's on us to show better preemption handling.
[01:51] Kara Bennett: small question — Dedicated pool. we thought Dedicated had better isolation; can you explain the preemption scenario?
[01:58] Maya Chen: good callout. Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor risk but autoscaling/maintenance hooks can still cause transient evictions depending on instance type and cloud provider. we've been tuning lifecycle hooks to avoid evicting hot KV caches during business hours.
[02:10] Ethan Park: on the latency incident: most of the 99th spikes correlated with cache misses and unusually long batching windows; when batching waits for more requests to fill GPUs the per-request latency can increase for tail calls.
[02:23] Liam O'Neill: so batching is a double-edged sword — saves cost but hurts 99th. can we set a max batch latency?
[02:29] Priya Nair: yes, we expose a max-wait-ms and a target-batch-size. lowering wait reduces cost savings but improves SLOs. we suggested a hybrid config for your peak hours.
[02:38] Ravi Desai: curious about model quantization suggestions — any quick wins? we saw notes about q4fp16 and 4-bit mixes.
[02:44] Ethan Park: for your workload the model family you are using is amenable to int4 quantization with small accuracy tradeoffs. Redwood Optimize can run an automated evaluation and show token cost savings. we'll include those numbers in the pricing scenarios.
[02:56] Kara Bennett: on security: procurement wants to see SOC2 scope and HSM/KMS integration docs. we listed that in the RFP.
[03:03] Jordan Li: we'll share our security pack — SOC2 + ISO certs, and KMS patterns we support. note: for Private deployments we can support customer-managed HSM; Hosted can integrate via customer KMS in supported clouds.
[03:16] Sofia Martinez: ideal is HSM with audit log exports. is the audit logging granular enough?
[03:20] Jordan Li: yes, we capture token-level traces, request/response metadata (redacted) and user actions in the console. logs can be exported to your SIEM — we'll attach the runbook.
[03:30] Maya Chen: let's walk through the pricing scenarios quickly — dedicated commit with reserved GPUs vs hosted on-demand. Ethan, you wanna take that?
[03:37] Ethan Park: Sure. Scenario A: Hosted on-demand — pay per token, no commit; higher per-token unit but flexible. Scenario B: Dedicated reserved — monthly commit with lower unit cost, but you pay for the reserved pool even if underutilized. Scenario C: Hybrid routing — critical routes go to Dedicated, burst to Hosted; complexity in routing but good balance.
[03:58] Kara Bennett: can you quantify per 1M tokens in these scenarios, ballpark?
[04:03] Ethan Park: ballpark now: Hosted $150 - $210 per 1M tokens depending on model variant and latency tier; Dedicated baseline about $110 - $140 per 1M tokens after amortized GPU cost and utilization assumptions. these are illustrative; we'll send a spreadsheet with your specific traffic profile.
[04:20] Liam O'Neill: those buckets matter. our finance needs scenarios with 50/70/90% utilization assumptions.
[04:26] Maya Chen: we'll provide three utilization modeled scenarios.
[04:29] Ravi Desai: pilot scope — we want to validate latency & correctness across 60 days. success metrics: 95th < 300ms, 99th < 800ms, cost < $X per 1M tokens (we'll share X).
[04:42] Priya Nair: good. we recommend a canary rollout with A/B for 10% -> 50% -> 100% windows and auto-fallback to hosted variant on SLO breach.
[04:54] Kara Bennett: re: fallback, how quick is the route switch?
[04:57] Ethan Park: route switch can be immediate via control plane flag; typically under 5s to flip traffic to the fallback model. stateful sessions will be rehydrated as needed — there is some lag for KV cache warmup.
[05:10] Liam O'Neill: cache warmup is a concern — can you pre-warm?
[05:13] Priya Nair: yes, pre-warm by replaying representative prefixes; we can run a warm-start job before big rollouts. we'll need your sample traffic.
[05:21] Ravi Desai: speaking of sample traffic, Kara will send that CSV.
[05:24] Kara Bennett: yes, I'll send the CSV after the call.
[05:27] Jordan Li: for the benchmark, Ethan will run tail-latency tests using your corpus on both Hosted and Dedicated with the same model checkpoint. expect a spreadsheet with 50/95/99 percentiles and cost per million.
[05:38] Ethan Park: yep. also we'll include two quantization profiles: int8 baseline and int4 experimental.
[05:44] Ravi Desai: any known issues with int4 on our model family?
[05:47] Ethan Park: small accuracy drift on certain rare prompts — we'll run evaluations on your eval set and highlight regressions. if regressions exceed your threshold we won't recommend int4 for those endpoints.
[05:58] Maya Chen: procurement items — Sofia, do you need a draft contract or SOW?
[06:02] Sofia Martinez: draft SOW plus pricing table and security pack. our internal review needs those before 11/17.
[06:08] Maya Chen: we'll get those to you.
[06:10] Kara Bennett: quick question on monitoring: do you support token-level cost attribution by route and model version?
[06:16] Jordan Li: yes, Console gives per-route, per-model token and latency breakdowns; we'll show you the console view live in the pilot.
[06:24] Liam O'Neill: are there any upcoming maintenance windows that could impact Dedicated?
[06:29] Priya Nair: we have an upcoming infra patch on 11/20 for some host kernels; we'll avoid evicting Dedicated pools during business hours if the customer requests it. we can schedule maintenance off-window for Aquarelle.
[06:41] Ravi Desai: good. what about data residency? some of our EU users require EU-only processing.
[06:46] Maya Chen: we support region pinning. for Hosted we can route EU traffic to EU data centers; for Private you can run in your VPC in-region. we'll document routing rules.
[06:57] Kara Bennett: competitor check: InferEdge suggested a fully on-prem snackable runtime but had limited console telemetry; CloudModelX pushed a cheaper headline price but no quantization validation.
[07:09] Maya Chen: helpful — we'll call that out in the proposal.
[07:12] Ravi Desai: last thing on rollout priorities: we want feature X first, then feature Y. can you map UX-impacting endpoints to low-latency priority buckets?
[07:22] Ethan Park: we can do that — if you mark the endpoints we'll map priority, recommended Dedicated allocation, and fallback policy.
[07:29] Kara Bennett: I'll annotate the list and send to Maya.
[07:32] Maya Chen: great. recap of next steps: Ethan to run benchmarks; Maya to send pricing and SOW; Jordan to share security pack; Kara to send traffic CSV and endpoint priority; Aquarelle to decide pilot metrics by 11/17. any objections?
[07:47] Ravi Desai: sounds good.
[07:49] Sofia Martinez: agreed.
[07:50] Maya Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and a 30-minute pilot kickoff once the documents are shared.
[07:59] Liam O'Neill: thanks all.
[08:01] Maya Chen: bye.

--- End transcript ---
